question: According to Mendeleev's periodic table, which unknown element of group III had an atomic mass of 68 that was later replaced by gallium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Eka–aluminum.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It was later discovered as Aluminium with an **atomic weight of 68 and an atomic number of 31. Germanium was named as ****Aka-Silicon first and was later discovered.**
 
• Eka prefix means that element occurring after suffix atom. It Means Eka aluminium is Gallium and Eka silicon is Germanium.
 
• One of these elements was the element now called Germanium; Mendeleev called it “eka-silicon,” meaning “beyond silicon” on his table.
 
• The existence of germanium was predicted by Dimitri Mendeleev in 1869 from a blank space in his periodic table beneath silicon; hence the term eka-silicon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6e0f4a473a5595c90984bc3f6183e95e85475b2b5ca3a6d6f2e1afba5f12e3b.png]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Ekamanganese (uncountable) (chemistry) is the name given by Dmitri Mendeleev to the predicted element (technetium) lying below manganese in the periodic table.
 
• Eka-aluminium was the name given by Mendeleev to the undiscovered element which now exists by the name of Gallium. Gallium belongs to group 13 of the periodic table. Its atomic number is 31 with the sign Ga. It is a soft, silvery metal at standard temperature and pressure.
 
• **Ekaboron (uncountable) (chemistry) is the name given by Dmitri Mendeleev to the predicted element (scandium) lying below the boron in the periodic table.**
